Let
\[
A=k[x]/(x^{2m+1}).
\]
Since \(x^{2m+1}=0\), the element \(1+x\) is invertible. The defining relation is therefore equivalent to
\[
yx=-\frac{x}{1+x}\,y.
\]
Define
\[
\sigma:A\to A,\qquad \sigma(x)=-\frac{x}{1+x}.
\]
Then \(\sigma^2=\mathrm{id}\), since
\[
\sigma(\sigma(x))=-\frac{-x/(1+x)}{1-x/(1+x)}=x.
\]
Thus
\[
R_m \cong A[y;\sigma],
\]
the skew polynomial algebra with rule \(ya=\sigma(a)y\) for \(a\in A\). Every element has a unique form
\[
z=\sum_{j\ge 0} a_j y^j,\qquad a_j\in A.
\]

Now impose centrality. First, \(z\) commutes with \(x\) iff
\[
a_j\sigma^j(x)=xa_j
\]
for every \(j\). Since \(A\) is commutative, this gives no condition for even \(j\). For odd \(j\), it gives
\[
a_j(\sigma(x)-x)=0.
\]
But
\[
\sigma(x)-x=-\frac{x}{1+x}-x=-\frac{x(2+x)}{1+x},
\]
and \((1+x),(2+x)\) are units in \(A\), so this is equivalent to
\[
a_jx=0.
\]
In \(A=k[x]/(x^{2m+1})\), the annihilator of \(x\) is \(kx^{2m}\). Hence for odd \(j\),
\[
a_j\in kx^{2m}.
\]

Second, \(z\) commutes with \(y\) iff
\[
a_j=\sigma(a_j)
\]
for every \(j\). So even coefficients must lie in \(A^\sigma\), while odd coefficients are scalar multiples of \(x^{2m}\), which is fixed by \(\sigma\) because
\[
\sigma(x^{2m})=\left(-\frac{x}{1+x}\right)^{2m}
=x^{2m}(1+x)^{-2m}=x^{2m}
\]
modulo \(x^{2m+1}\).

It remains to describe \(A^\sigma\). Put
\[
u=\frac{x}{x+2}.
\]
This is valid since \(x+2\) is a unit. Then
\[
\sigma(u)=\frac{\sigma(x)}{\sigma(x)+2}
=\frac{-x/(1+x)}{-x/(1+x)+2}
=-\frac{x}{x+2}
=-u.
\]
Also \(A=k[u]/(u^{2m+1})\). Therefore the \(\sigma\)-invariants are exactly the even polynomials in \(u\):
\[
A^\sigma=k[u^2]=k\left[\left(\frac{x}{x+2}\right)^2\right].
\]

Thus the center consists of arbitrary polynomials in \(u^2\) and \(y^2\), together with the odd central part generated by \(x^{2m}y\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{
Z(R_m)=k\left[\left(\frac{x}{x+2}\right)^2,\ y^2,\ x^{2m}y\right]
}
\]
as a \(k\)-subalgebra of \(R_m\), where \((x+2)^{-1}\) is interpreted inside \(k[x]/(x^{2m+1})\). Equivalently,
\[
Z(R_m)=k\left[\left(\frac{x}{x+2}\right)^2,y^2\right]
\oplus x^{2m}y\,k[y^2].
\]
